cleaning.content: Always wash your hands with antibacterial soap before touching your tattoo. Then, with clean hands under warm water, wash your tattoo with antibacterial soap. Never rub your tattoo with a towel, but pat it dry with a kitchen towel. When the tattoo is dry, apply a thin layer of cream recommended by your tattoo artist.

list.1: During the first week after tattooing, special attention should be paid to regular washing and moisturizing of the tattoo, while avoiding activities that could irritate the skin, such as sports, sun exposure, sauna, solarium, swimming and unclean activities. The tattoo should be lubricated and washed 2-3 times a day.
list.2: During this period, the tattoo will begin to peel, which is a completely normal healing process. You will also feel a slight itch, but it is important not to pick at the dried paint particles from a fresh tattoo. If the itching is unbearable, it is recommended to gently wash and apply ointment, which will help soothe the skin.
list.3: In the second week, you can reduce the frequency of washing and lubricating the tattoo to 1-2 times a day, adapting to the needs of your skin. You can resume sports training, washing the tattoo thoroughly after each workout and applying ointment if necessary. You will gradually notice the skin and itching calming down.
list.4: The time it takes for a tattoo to heal can vary depending on a variety of factors, including the size of the tattoo, its location on the body, the individual's health, the care and maintenance of the tattoo, and the natural healing rate of the skin. In general, a tattoo can heal in 1-2 months. The tattoo is healed when it no longer peels and feels the same as the rest of the untattooed skin.
list.description: Caring for a fresh tattoo is crucial to ensuring successful healing and long-lasting durability of the artwork on the skin.

cleaning.title: Washing and lubricating the tattoo

list.1: Use the care cream recommended by your tattoo artist (Easytattoo, Bepanthen ointment, Tattoo care, Balea Tattoo).
list.2: Wear loose clothing made of natural materials over a fresh tattoo to avoid irritating and rubbing the tattoo.
list.3: It's best to keep the tattoo in the fresh air as much as possible.

others.note: Your care is crucial to how your tattoo will look for the rest of your life, so I recommend that you follow the instructions. When the tattoo is fully healed, please send me a photo of the tattoo or arrange to have it checked in the studio. You can find the contact details of each tattoo artist on the website tinta.tattoo.
others.title: Other instructions

recreation.content: Avoid any sports exercise and sweating for at least 10 days. Avoid swimming and other immersion in water, the sea or a swimming pool, and saunas for one month.
recreation.title: Sports training, swimming and sauna

removingFoil.content: Unwrap the tattoo with regular cling film after 3-5 hours. The tattoo with second skin film remains wrapped for 1-3 days. Remove the film under a warm shower. Remove the film by stretching it along the skin. Once the film is peeled off, wash the tattoo under warm water with antibacterial soap and gently dry it with a kitchen towel, being careful not to rub.
removingFoil.title: Removing the foil

sunbathing.content: We do not expose the tattoo to UV rays for at least the first month. Even when the tattoo is healed, it still needs to be taken care of if you want it to be beautiful and intense for a long time. In the long term, exposing the tattoo to UV rays breaks down the pigment trapped under the skin, so sunbathing contributes to the aging and fading of the tattoo. If you are going to be in the sun, it is necessary to apply a cream with a protection factor of 30-50 spf every few hours.
sunbathing.title: Sunbathing and solarium

3.answer: First, you need to have a rough idea of what you want to get tattooed. Based on your preferences, choose a tattoo artist whose style you like best and contact them. See the booking instructions. Before getting tattooed, read the tattooing instructions and customer etiquette. Before deciding on a tattoo, it is always a good idea to consult with the tattoo artist. Discussing your ideas, wishes and expectations will enable better understanding and cooperation between you and the tattoo artist and allow you to create a tattoo that is unique. On the day of your appointment, you will fill out a tattoo consent form, confirm the design, determine the exact location and size of the tattoo, and print the stencil. The tattoo artist will prepare your skin (shave, disinfect) and apply the stencil. Once you have confirmed that everything is as you want it, the tattooing process will begin. Once the tattoo is complete, a protective film is applied over it. Then, carefully follow the aftercare instructions. In rare cases, a tattoo may need to be touched up. If you need a touch-up, contact your tattoo artist and make an appointment for a free correction.
3.question: How does tattooing work?

qa.answer: Healing is an organic bodily process, which is why tattoo corrections are sometimes necessary. The body perceives pigment as a foreign substance and attempts to digest it through the lymphatic system during the healing process. Sometimes the body manages to break down the pigment particles and flush them out of the body. Especially with delicate, small tattoos or large areas of colour, it often happens that the tattoo is paler in certain areas than in others. If you have followed the aftercare instructions, you are entitled to one free repair within the first 6 months after tattooing. Do not delay and contact your tattoo artist to make your tattoo flawless.
qa.question: Repairs

risks.description: It is important to distinguish between the normal inflammatory process after tattooing and the risks and health complications that occur in very rare cases.

1.answer: Allergic reactions to pigment are rare. Inform your tattoo artist if you have any allergies, sensitivity to metals, condoms or latex.
1.question: Allergic reaction

2.answer: Granulomas and keloid scars are rare complications of tattooing. In most cases, they are the result of the work of an inexperienced tattoo artist or a pre-existing tendency to develop scar tissue.
2.question: Granulomas and keloid scars

3.answer: Due to the health and sanitary conditions in our studio, the risk of infection with blood-borne diseases or bacterial infections is almost impossible. Bacterial infection is a common reaction if you do not follow the aftercare instructions.

instructions.description: To make your new tattoo as beautiful as possible and to ensure that the tattooing process goes smoothly, we advise you to follow the recommendations below on how to care for your skin before the tattooing process itself.

items.1: Please come alone or with a small group, as there are more of us in the studio and it can get crowded quickly (except for parents and guardians signing the consent form). A small group may come to the appointment, as long as they do not disrupt the work process.
items.2: Come to the tattoo rested, well-fed, and hydrated.
items.3: Come to the tattoo shop clean, washed, and fragrant.
items.4: Do not come to the tattoo shop if you are sick or have a cold.
items.5: Wear comfortable, loose-fitting everyday clothing so that the tattoo artist can reach the tattoo site more easily and you will be more comfortable during the tattooing process.
items.6: For longer appointments, bring plenty of fluids (sweet drinks) and snacks.

day.note: If you have any illnesses, allergies, or are taking medication, please consult your doctor or contact us.
day.title: On tattoo day

items.1: Be punctual or at most 5 minutes early.
items.2: Do not come to your appointment if you are sick or have a cold.
items.3: Trust your tattoo artist if they tell you something isn't feasible, won't last long, or won't look good.
items.4: Don't be afraid to ask if the stencil can be moved, enlarged, reduced, changed. We are here to help and accommodate you. We understand that tattoos are permanent, so we ask that you express your wishes while changes are still possible. Express your fears, doubts, discomfort.
items.5: If you want to document and share the tattooing process and your experience on your phone, ask the tattoo artist for permission first.
items.6: During the tattooing process, please inform us about your well-being. Express your needs for food, drink, and breaks. Let us know if you feel dizzy, nauseous, sweat excessively, or are shaking. Let us know if you are cold or too hot. Let us know if the pain is too severe.
items.7: A small group of people may come to the appointment, as long as they do not disrupt the work process itself.
items.8: In case of cancellation or concerns, please let us know.

items.1: Don't sunbathe, don't go to a tanning bed.
Do not consume drugs or alcohol for at least 24 hours before tattooing (it causes excessive bleeding and makes healing difficult - scabs).
items.2: Do not shave or depilate the tattoo site to avoid further irritating the skin.
items.3: You can apply body milk/lotion to the tattoo site several times if you have dry skin, but do not apply 1 day before the tattoo.
items.4: For extremely dry skin, exfoliate the tattoo area daily for three days before your tattoo and apply moisturizer. This will help the skin become more supple and pliable.

about.content: We are a team of experienced tattoo artists who see art as a means of expression and connection. The most important thing for us is to create quality tattoos that last a lifetime. In our studio, we adhere to the highest hygiene standards to provide you with a tattoo that is safe for your health.
about.title: About us

artists.content1: We are constantly pushing the boundaries of creativity, looking for new ways to experiment and think outside the box. We love innovation, embracing unconventional ideas and techniques to bring your vision to life. We constantly invest in quality development and the expertise of our team.
artists.content2: Our diverse backgrounds and artistic styles allow us to cater to a wide range of preferences. We know that each individual is unique, so we strive to create a unique piece of art designed specifically for them. Whether you are looking for a traditional painting or a contemporary masterpiece, we have the expertise and imagination to exceed your expectations.

lana.bio: My tattoo style is defined by a variety of lines, lots of black areas, strong contrasts, fine details and soft shadows. I enjoy creating a variety of motifs, which I can add my own touch to and thus present in my own unique way. I am fascinated by mythological and mystical themes, I try to bring elements of magic and nature into my tattoos. The goal of my tattoos is to be as fluid and harmonious as possible with every body I get on canvas.
lana.name: Lana

milly.bio:
Milan is a versatile tattoo artist, specializing in black and grey realism and fineline realism. He places great importance on creating long-lasting, quality tattoos. With his knowledge of composition, anatomy, shapes and other artistic elements that define a quality piece, he always helps his clients create the desired motif exactly as they imagined it.
He says about his work:
Tattooing is a way for me to connect with the world. The way artists help people express themselves through tattoos is unique. The artist is constantly trying to find a balance to express themselves through their skin. Artists create symbolic or abstract forms on people and open up and elevate what people feel or think deep inside their skin. Nowadays, everyone has at least a small piece of skin covered in ink, and it's amazing!

"I love getting up every morning and doing what I love."
milly.name: Milan
